sentences.en: From headline-grabbing Ponzi schemes, to email phishing identity thieves, to fake news stories
sentences.zh: 从耸人听闻的庞氏骗局，到电子邮件钓鱼身份窃贼，再到在社交媒体上流传的

sentences.en: circulating on social media, it can sometimes seem like the world is full of people who want to deceive us.
sentences.zh: 假新闻故事，有时看起来世界充满了想要欺骗我们的人。

sentences.en: What many of these scammers and con artists have in common is that they take advantage of the patterns of thinking and the mental shortcuts that we all use in our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 许多这类骗子和江湖郎中所共有的特点是，他们利用了我们所有人日常生活中都在使用的思维模式和心理捷径。

sentences.en: Most of the time, these mental habits serve us well.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，这些心理习惯对我们很有帮助。

sentences.en: After all, most people aren't trying to trick us and it would be difficult to go through life skeptical of everything and everyone.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，大多数人并不是在试图欺骗我们，如果对所有人和事都抱着怀疑态度，生活将难以维系。

sentences.en: But the same habits of trust and belief that work well most of the time can leave us vulnerable when we encounter a con artist, a false news story, or some other type of deceit.
sentences.zh: 但正是这种在多数情况下运转良好的信任与信念习惯，当我们在遇到骗子、虚假新闻故事或其他类型的欺骗时，会让我们变得不堪一击。

sentences.en: So what are the cognitive habits that put us at risk of believing lies and falling prey to scams?

sentences.en: Are some people simply more gullible than others or can anyone be conned?
sentences.zh: 是否有些人天生就比其他人更好骗，还是说任何人都有可能被骗？

sentences.en: When you're offered something that sounds like an amazing opportunity, what questions should you ask to figure out if it's too good to be true?
sentences.zh: 当有人向你提供听起来像是一个绝佳机会的东西时，你应该问自己哪些问题来判断它是否好得不真实？

sentences.en: How common is fraud in the worlds of business, science, and elsewhere?

sentences.en: Why is it that we're all vulnerable to being deceived at least some of the time?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们所有人在至少某些时候都容易受到欺骗？

sentences.en: I think we tend to think that only the most gullible among us can be deceived.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们倾向于认为只有我们当中最容易轻信的人才会被骗。

sentences.en: And there's good reason for that.
sentences.zh: 这有充分的理由。

sentences.en: Whenever you hear about a scam or you hear about somebody falling for a con, in retrospect, it seems obvious.
sentences.zh: 每当你听到关于骗局的消息或听说有人上当受骗时，事后看来，这一切似乎都显而易见。

sentences.en: And you can think to yourself, oh yeah, I wouldn't have fallen for that.
sentences.zh: 你可能会心想，哦，是的，我才不会上当呢。

sentences.en: But most scams aren't targeting you.
sentences.zh: 但大多数骗局并不是针对你的。

sentences.en: They're targeting somebody.
sentences.zh: 它们是针对某个人的。

sentences.en: And when a scam is really targeted to you in particular, that meets your desires, your wishes, your wants, you're more likely to fall for it than if it's not.
sentences.zh: 而当一个骗局真正特别针对你、迎合你的渴望、你的愿望、你的需求时，你比在它没有针对你时更有可能上当受骗。

sentences.en: So we all can be subject to being deceived if the targeting is aimed at us, and it takes advantage of the way we think and the information we're looking for.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果定向针对我们，并且它利用了我们的思维方式以及我们正在寻找的信息，我们所有人都可能会遭到欺骗。

sentences.en: So Dr. Chivry, let me ask you, what are some of the most common cognitive shortcuts or thinking patterns that get us into trouble?
sentences.zh: 那么查布里斯博士，请问是什么让我们陷入麻烦的最常见认知捷径或思维模式有哪些？

sentences.en: I think the first one that we talk about is
sentences.zh: 我认为我们讨论的第一个是

sentences.en: truth bias.
sentences.zh: 真实偏误。

sentences.en: So truth bias is the idea that our default tendency is to think that whatever we hear or read or encounter is true, that people are not always trying to lie to us or deceive us.
sentences.zh: 真实偏误是指这样一种观点：我们的默认倾向是认为我们听到、读到或遇到的一切都是真的，人们并不总是试图对我们说谎或欺骗我们。

sentences.en: And that's sort of a precondition for being taken in by any kind of scam or con or fraud.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是被任何类型的骗局、诈骗或欺诈所蒙蔽的前提条件。

sentences.en: Because if you believed everything you saw was false or questionable or misleading, then you wouldn't
sentences.zh: 因为如果你相信你看到的一切都是假的、可疑的或具有误导性的，那么你就

sentences.en: really act on those offers and those promises and those sales pitches and those marketing messages.
sentences.zh: 不会真正对那些报价、承诺、推销和营销信息采取行动。

sentences.en: And truth bias is important for us to have because if we didn't tend to accept what other people said,
sentences.zh: 我们需要真实偏误，因为如果我们不倾向于接受别人所说的话，

sentences.en: we'd never be able to make plans with them, have a conversation with them, or do anything
sentences.zh: 我们就永远无法与他们制定计划、与他们交谈，或者做任何事情，

sentences.en: really other than be skeptical all the time.
sentences.zh: 除了整天保持怀疑之外别无他法。

sentences.en: Once you start with truth bias, then other cognitive habits we have can get us into further trouble.
sentences.zh: 一旦你从真实偏误开始，我们拥有的其他认知习惯就会给我们带来进一步的麻烦。

sentences.en: And I guess one I would highlight to start with is our habit of focus, which refers to our tendency to focus on information that's right in front of
sentences.zh: 我想首先强调的一个是我们的专注习惯，它指的是我们倾向于关注眼前、

sentences.en: us that we have easily at hand, often that someone has provided to us, and make decisions based only
sentences.zh: 手头容易获得的信息（通常是别人提供给我们的），并且仅根据这些信息

sentences.en: on that information, operating essentially under the assumption that that's all that matters or that's all there is.
sentences.zh: 做出决策，基本上在“这就是全部重要内容”或“这就是全部”的假设下运作。

sentences.en: And one of the main ways to avoid being deceived is to think about information that people aren't showing you or information that's missing or has been withheld, or you're just not
sentences.zh: 避免被骗的主要方法之一，是去思考别人没有向你展示的信息、缺失或被隐瞒的信息，或者你只是没有

sentences.en: thinking about broadening your focus to include other information besides perhaps what the scam or a con artist wants you to be focusing on at that particular moment.
sentences.zh: 考虑到拓宽你的视野，去包含除了特定时刻骗子或江湖郎中想让你关注的信息之外的其他信息。

sentences.en: So it's especially easy to fool people when you tell them something that they want to believe anyway, or something that matches the preconceived notion.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你告诉人们他们无论如何都想相信的事情，或者符合先入为主观念的事情时，尤其容易愚弄他们。

sentences.en: So how can we fall into the trap of not being willing to reexamine our own beliefs?
sentences.zh: 那么我们怎么会陷入不愿意重新审视自己信念的陷阱呢？

sentences.en: This is a general issue, right?

sentences.en: That we tend to make predictions about the world.

sentences.en: We have to, right?

sentences.en: And most of the time, that's a great thing to do.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，这是一件很棒的事情。

sentences.en: And that's true for most of these sort of cognitive tendencies.
